thread:
alex_k: Running a controlled FP8 rollout on H100 + L40S. After calibration pass, we see intermittent quality blips on long-context traces and a correlated spike in kernel fallback counts. Posting traces + quick repro.

maria: thanks alex — can you paste the transformer-engine flags you're using? are we running precompile or on-demand? :thinking_face:

alex_k: here are the runtime flags for the failing job (defaults come from canary profile):

```
runtime_config: {
  use_triton_kernels: true
  te_precompile: true
  nvfuser_path: /opt/nvfuser
  quant_mode: fp8_auto_calib
  calib_samples: 1024
  kv_cache_max_entries: 131072
  batch_shape: dynamic
}
```

jon: attached a condensed nsys slice — kernel chosen flips between fp8_matmul_v2 and int8_safe_matmul depending on sequence length. when FP8 kernel wins, latency drops ~18% but logit L2 distance vs FP32 drifts by ~0.03 at step ~1023. snippet: 

```
# nsys summary (slice)
kernel, count, avg_ms
fp8_matmul_v2, 37, 0.42
int8_safe_matmul, 21, 0.52
kv_read, 480, 0.0012
kv_eviction, 3, 0.85
```

jon: also saw `kv_eviction` only on the H100 runs with aggressive batching (microbatch sizes variable).

sophia: that eviction number 3 is worrying — could be due to cached prefix addresses being recycled when microbatch shapes vary. We recently changed the batcher to maximize occupancy which ups burst size.

sam: quick experiment idea: set `te_precompile=false` and `use_triton_kernels=false` to force the nvfuser path on H100 and see if the calibration drift persists. If drift disappears, it points at TE kernel FP8 implementation/quant params.

alex_k: ran that exact experiment on H100. Results: fallback->int8 count dropped 75%, but we still see logit drift in ~2% of sequences (mostly >2048 tokens). Throughput changed: FP8-nvfuser = 11.6k tok/s, FP8-TE = 14.2k tok/s, INT8 fallback = 9.8k tok/s.

maria: interesting. so TE gives better perf but higher instability in long-context. do we have calibration histograms? maybe the scale factor tails for long kv keys are clipping.

alex_k: pasted simplified calib histograms (max per-layer scale) from the same job: 

```
layer_3: {p5: 0.004, p50: 0.012, p95: 0.09}
layer_11: {p5: 0.002, p50: 0.01, p95: 0.4}  # suspicious heavy tail
layer_17: {p5: 0.003, p50: 0.011, p95: 0.06}
```

alex_k: layer_11 tail jumps when sequence > 2k, aligns with the logit drift.

jon: could be numerical accumulators in TE kernel for KV writes reading stale scales under multi-stream concurrency. I have a diff that adds a per-stream scale barrier — low risk. Want me to land for canary?

maria: before landing, we should reproduce consistently. Steps I propose:
1) reproduce with te_precompile=true and te_precompile=false on both H100 & L40S
2) run a debug job with `KV_DEBUG=true` that logs `kv.eviction_count`, `kv.write_scale` per-layer per-step
3) run 10 seeds for the long-context eval set (same prompts) and compute logit L2 and BLEU-like metric

sam: +1. also try raising `kv_cache_max_entries` to 262144 for H100 canary to see if eviction disappears (cheap config change).

alex_k: doing the matrix: H100/L40S x precompile on/off x kv_cache size 131k/262k x 3 seeds. kicking off now — I pushed a job: <link to job: https://infra/jobs/3160001111> 

deploy-bot: CI job 3160001111 started on cluster-canary-h100 (profile: fp8-canary) :rocket:

infra-bot: note: if the larger kv cache avoids evictions but doesn't fix the drift, that points at quant scale instability rather than eviction race. I'll reserve extra memory on node pool so we can test 262k entries without impacting other tenants.

sophia: small additional check — try setting `batcher.max_microbatch_variation=0` to force consistent microbatch shapes for the run. If drift disappears, the root cause is the batcher reshaping leading to mis-indexed KV pointers.

alex_k: early results in: H100 + te_precompile=true + kv=131k + variable microbatches => logit drift rate 2.1% (baseline). H100 + te_precompile=true + kv=262k + fixed microbatch => drift 0.3%. L40S runs never showed >0.4% drift in any config so far.

maria: that is telling: H100 + precompile + variable microbatch -> correlated failures. TE precompile likely triggers a fast path that isn't handling microbatch reshapes + FP8 scale recompute.

jon: I'll open a small PR that adds a scale recompute barrier in the TE fp8 matmul fast-path and a microbatch-sanity-check when writing KV indices. I'll also add more telemetry counters: `kv.write_scale_mismatch` and `kernel.scale_recompute_count`.

alex_k: thanks — action items:
- jon PR and canary run (jon)
- infra to keep enlarged kv pool for tests (infra-bot)
- sam to run extended perf sweep to quantify perf delta TE vs nvfuser post-fix (sam)
- maria to collect calibration histograms across layers every 256 steps (maria)

sam: noted. If PR reduces drift but perf regresses >8% vs TE baseline, we'll discuss compensating with batching heuristics (smarter burst packing) to recover throughput.

alex_k: cool. leaving the job running. Will report back with PR link + new traces. :white_check_mark:
